relations.evidence: Bhūpatīndramalla devasana ñalāyā śrīśrīIndramalladevasake ... vāṅāyā dharota

purpose: Record (dharoṭa) of what Bhūpatīndra Malla sent to Indra Malla when the Gaurīvivāha dance-drama was performed
notes: No scribe is named. The quoted colophon contains no date and no place. The catalogue gives NS 827 pauṣa śukla tṛtīyā śukravāra (≈1707 CE) and Bhaktapur, so those details probably come from elsewhere in the manuscript. The text reads as a record of goods 'sent' (vāṅāyā) by King Bhūpatīndra Malla of Bhaktapur (instrumental -sana) to Indra Malla (-sake 'to') on the occasion of the Gaurīvivāha pyākhan. 'ñalāyā' is probably a corruption or misreading of 'yalāyā' ('of Yala', i.e. Patan). That fits Indra Malla, who ruled Patan briefly around NS 826–829. Bhūpatīndra's role is a mix of king and sender/commissioner of the document; Indra Malla is the recipient, not the reigning king of the place where it was copied.
